crime: Every evening, a girl played pool alone in the recreation room, talking the whole time to {WITCH_NAME}, who sat faded out of sight on the bench against the wall. {WITCH_NAME} never stayed for a goodbye. Before anyone could say one, she slipped out unseen, and the door swung open by itself. Every time, the girl called goodbye after the door.

Tonight, the girl reached the bench first. She took {WITCH_NAME}'s hand and said goodbye, slowly. {WITCH_NAME}'s mother had once held that hand and said goodbye just as slowly, every morning for a week. On the eighth morning, her mother was gone.

{WITCH_NAME} opened the door and let it swing shut, but stayed in the room. "See you tomorrow!" the girl called after it. As she bent over the table to take her shot, {WITCH_NAME} slammed her head into the pool table until the girl lay still.

Out in the second-floor hall, the prisoners heard "See you tomorrow" and watched the recreation room door until the lockup call. No one came out. In the trial court, they ruled that the girl had slipped while playing alone and struck her head on the pool table.

Then the prisoner who had found her remembered sinking onto the bench against the wall. It had still been warm. The prisoners understood at last: {WITCH_NAME} had sat there, faded out of sight, until they walked in.
fields.epitaph: The one time she stayed after a goodbye, it had only meant tomorrow.
execution: In the trial court, an iron doorway stood on the execution stand. She was chained upright inside it, one wrist fastened to each side of the frame. The iron door swung shut on its own, into her head and chest. It swung open and shut again, and again, and again. When it finally came to rest, it hung ajar against her slumped body. It could not close.

magic.name: Fade Out
magic.text: She can fade out of sight, clothes and all, while staying right where she is.
